title: Ops probe scripts and dashboard axioms
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working note for small, repeatable probe scripts (synthetic and lightweight real-traffic probes), the minimum metric/trace schema they should emit, and a short set of dashboard axioms that let oncall quickly reason about tokenized inference degradation. Focus is practical: cheap probes, easy dashboard glances, and fast tracer-guided investigation paths.

Quick background/context:
- We run a mix of synthetic probes (scheduled, controlled prompts) and opportunistic micro-probes (short recordings emitted alongside production requests for sampling).
- Objective: detect regressions in latency, first-byte time, kv-cache-effectiveness, and output-quality divergence early enough to triage before customer-visible SLO breaches.

Probe choreography (scripts):
1) hourly-smoke-mini: low-cost synthetic run (4 prompts, 3 model variants)
   - cadence: every hour per region
   - cost target: < 0.02 USD/hr per region
   - outputs: latency_ms (p50/p95), ttfb_ms, tokens_generated, model_variant, prompt_id, probe_id
   - success heuristic: p95 latency < configured SLO and ttfb_ms < baseline*1.5

2) kv-warmth-sample: prefix-warmth focused probe (warm then cold path)
   - cadence: run once per 6 hours staggered across shards
   - emit: kv_hit_rate (0..1), kv_prefetch_latency_ms, eviction_hint (boolean), prefix_hash
   - expected: warm path kv_hit_rate > 0.8 after pre-warm; cold path informs eviction/backoff tuning

3) token-path-heat: multi-length token generation to exercise slow path (long vs short sequences)
   - cadence: nightly, run only on dedicated test pool to avoid noise
   - emit: per-token-latency_ms (array as summarised p50/p90/p99), kv_cache_size, stage (compilation/warmup/steady)

Minimum metric schema (for probes and production tags):
- metric name: inference.request.latency_ms
  - description: end-to-end request latency measured at serving API ingress (ms)
  - labels: model, model_variant, region, customer_tier, probe_id (optional), session_id (optional)
  - aggregation: p50/p90/p95/p99, count, rate per minute

- metric name: inference.kv.hit_rate
  - description: fraction of prefix/KV cache lookups that hit the cache (0..1)
  - labels: model, region, pool_id, probe_type
  - aggregation: avg over 5m and 1h windows

- metric name: inference.ttfb_ms
  - description: time to first byte from serving runtime to client (ms)
  - labels: path (streaming|batch), model, region
  - alert if sustained p95 increase > baseline*1.4 for 30m

- metric name: inference.output.regression_score
  - description: lightweight quality score comparing model response to canonical expectations (0..1)
  - labels: prompt_id, model_variant, eval_set
  - aggregation: rolling 7d and anomaly detector feed

Tracing guidance (span and attribute conventions):
- Span naming: use stable, human-friendly anchors: ingress.http.request -> serving.runtime.call -> kv.cache.lookup -> op.kernel.exec -> egress.stream.write
- Each span MUST include attributes: model.name, model.variant, request.id, sequence.length, region, tenant.id (if available), session.slice (0/1/2)
- Sampling policy: weighted adaptive sampling. Guarantee 1 full-trace per 10k requests free-sample and always sample synthetic probes + traces that hit error codes or have latency > p95 threshold then mark as high-priority (sample=1).
- Trace breadcrumbs for debugging large fanouts: add attribute fanout.count and fanout.targets when a request fans out to multiple model variants or routing tiers.

Dashboard axioms (how to design panels so humans can decide fast):
Axiom 1: Every dashboard must have a single lead indicator at the top row — a compact sparkline + current p95 latency and delta vs baseline. If that panel is red, operators start here.
Axiom 2: Surface two orthogonal causes across rows: runtime performance (latency, cpu/gpu util, kernel stalls) and data-quality/regression (output score, stray prompt patterns).
Axiom 3: Show cardinality knobs: default view is aggregated; provide tenant/model selectors and a pre-baked top-10 tenants/model variants table.
Axiom 4: Provide triage anchors: a) top correlated traces (grouped by span name), b) top recent errors with sample traces, c) kv-warmth histogram.
Axiom 5: Keep panels lightweight — no more than 12 total widgets for a single SLO dashboard. Use linked drilldowns for long tail.

Suggested top-of-dashboard layout (compact):
- Row 1 (lead indicators): p95 latency sparkline, request rate, ttfb p95 delta
- Row 2 (triage buckets): top error codes, recent rollouts (model_variant tags), probe-failure count
- Row 3 (cache health): kv.hit_rate timeseries, eviction events, prefix-warmth index
- Row 4 (quality): output.regression_score trend, top failed prompts (sampled texts hashed), eval-drift alert line

Investigation runbook (3-10 minute path):
1) Confirm lead indicator red; switch to 15m window and verify signal in synthetic probe (if probe is green, likely production-specific or noisy).
2) If synthetic probe also red, check rollout tags: recent model_variant rollouts in last 60m. If rollout exists, roll back or initiate canary evaluation.
3) Pull the most recent high-latency traces (group by span op.kernel.exec or kv.cache.lookup).
4) For kernel stalls: inspect GPU util + kernel queue lengths. For kv issues: inspect kv.hit_rate by pool_id and eviction_hint attributes.
5) If output.regression_score dropped but latency normal: isolate model variant and run eval harness on canonical prompt set.
6) If no clear cause: collect a 5m trace bundle and escalate to infra/serving-runtime on-call with links to traces and probe IDs.

Alert heuristics (examples):
- Latency alert: p95 latency > SLO*1.25 for 15m AND probe_count_failed > 0 in same window -> severity P2
- Cache alert: kv_hit_rate < 0.6 for any dedicated pool for 10m -> severity P3
- Quality alert (early warning): anomaly detector flag on output.regression_score with > 3 sigma deviation AND > 10 failing prompts -> severity P2

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Probe cadence vs cost: prefer low-frequency synthetic probes that exercise edge-cases (kv cold path, long token sequences) and rely on sampled production traces to detect noisy signal shapes.
- Metric cardinality: avoid high-cardinality labels on high-volume metrics; use derived rollups for tenant-level troubleshooting.
- Sampling: always guarantee full traces for probes; for production, use adaptive sampling that biases on errors, latency, and new model variants.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical set of 10 probe prompts for cross-model quality checks (Sofia to propose list by 2025-02-25).
- Small library: a probe -> trace bundler (lightweight python util) to attach probe_id and collect contextual logs (Jonah owner).
- Evaluate adding a small model-side health ping metric (model.process.heap_free_mb) to help detect memory pressure stalls.

Appendix: shorthand definitions and quick lookups:
- prefix-warmth index: engineered metric (0..100) indicating how often prefixes are served from warm caches within a time window. Computed as (recent_warm_hits / recent_total_prefixes)*100. Use 5m and 1h windows.
- session.slice: small integer labeling whether trace corresponds to first request in session (0), follow-ups (1), or background/async (2).

Notes to self: keep this doc small and pragmatic. We will extract a clean checklist for oncall and a probe-templates repo once the prompt set is agreed.

End of doc.
